candidates.exact_span: As required by 40 CFR 127.16, all Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) shall be electronically reported. The monitoring results will be available to the public via EPA's Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO) web site at https://echo.epa.gov.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether DMR electronic submission is an applicable monitoring/reporting obligation for FY2025, and whether absence of results in ECHO should be treated as missing required evidence versus another documented no-data state, depends on how this requirement is interpreted and applied to the selected facilities and periods.

candidates.exact_span: The EPA approved 2018-2020 State of New Mexico CWA §303(d) / §305(b) Integrated Report identifies the receiving stream segment no, 20.6.4.401(San Juan River (Navajo Nation boundary at Hogback to Animas River) is impaired for turbidity sedimentation/siltation and E. coli bacteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identification of the receiving segment and its impairments for turbidity, sedimentation/siltation, and E. coli can affect which parameters have enforceable numeric limits versus report-only monitoring, and whether monitoring for those impairment-related parameters was required during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit proposes E. coli limits consistently with the approved TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of whether E. coli limits are TMDL-based enforceable numeric limits, and which limit values govern, would change which E. coli measurement/limit pairs are subject to compliance comparison under Purpose A.

candidates.exact_span: The standard reopener language in the permit allows additional permit conditions if warranted by future changes and/or new TMDLs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the reopener is interpreted as making limits or monitoring conditions contingent on future TMDL or water-quality changes, applicability of numeric limits and monitoring requirements for FY2025 could differ from a reading that treats existing proposed conditions as fixed.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed draft are developed from the appropriate State WQS and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether specific limits and monitoring duties are sourced from State WQS and therefore operative for compliance evaluation depends on interpreting this linkage; different readings could change which limits are treated as enforceable and which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the antibacksliding standard and whether any less-stringent draft limits are justified by facility alterations affects which numeric limits are enforceable for FY2025 compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit is slightly more restrictive than the previous permit since the Cyanide limits have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether newly established Cyanide limits are operative enforceable numeric limits (versus not yet effective or not applicable) changes which Cyanide measurements require limit comparison and whether Cyanide monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, the 30-day average TDS net incremental increase and loading limits have been revised downward to 449 mg/L (from 497 mg/L) and to 24,992 lbs/day (from 27,664 lbs/day), respectively, in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated revised TDS concentration and loading limits are specific numeric values whose applicability to FY2025 measurements directly determines compliance comparison outcomes under Purpose A.

candidates.exact_span: For other pollutants (i.e., BOD5, TSS, pH, E. coli, and TRC), their limits are kept the same.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A reading that these parameters retain prior-permit limits affects which numeric limits apply for FY2025 and whether monitoring for those parameters remained required unchanged from the previous permit term.

candidates.locator: page 17, fact_sheet, XV. ENDANGERED SPECIES CONSIDERATIONS
candidates.exact_span: According to the most recent county listing available at US Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), Southwest Region 2 website, http://ecos.fws.gov/tess_public/reports/species-by-current-range-county?fips=35045, ten species in San Juan County are listed as endangered (E), threatened (T)
candidates.computation_change_reason: If endangered-species presence triggers permit monitoring or reporting conditions, interpretation of this species listing reference could change whether certain monitoring was required in FY2025 and how missing related evidence should be classified when no ordinary numeric result is available.
